sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Commoners**, also known as , are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Lower-class citizens of Lands Between, commoners can be found in most major settlements. They no longer have their wits about them, and are typically hostile towards the Tarnished. They are most often seen wearing boards around their neck depicting a sprawling tree, with holes formed by its roots. This is a self-imposed shackle representing a voluntary display of allegiance to the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.markdown: Commoner=

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Commoners dressed in plain garb, bearing evidence of their devotion to the Erdtree on the boards hung around their necks. They fight using weathered straight swords, and will sometimes throw Fire Pots and Ruin Fragments.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Maddened commoners found in places touched by the frenzied flame, which can be seen burning in their eyes. They are found in the Ailing Village, Frenzied Flame Village, and Yelough Anix Ruins. They fight using swords and spears, and can harness the power of the frenzied flame to unleash Madness-inflicting attacks.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: White-haired necromancers found only in the Black Knife Catacombs. They dress in similar garb to commoners, but with black tunics, and they carry torchpoles blazing with a pale flame. They have the ability to continuously resurrect nearby Skeletons by preventing them from being permanently killed unless holy damage is used. If the necromancer is killed, all of the skeletons connected to them will also die.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Commoners clad only in ragged loincloths and headbands, found exclusively in Volcano Manor. They wield swords, torches, and spears, and will use Fire Pots, Poison Pots, Oil Pots and Ruin Fragments.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Catacombs** are recurring Landmarks in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Catacombs are maze-like, subterranean dungeons that include puzzles and have at least one Boss. They are accessed by locating and opening a door at their entrances in the overworld and descending elevators. They are almost always filled with traps and require the player to pull a lever to unlock the large door to the boss's arena, which bears a relief of a tree with corpses within its roots. They are typically guarded by Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, their Imp underlings, and Grave Warden Duelists.

These burial grounds were constructed in proximity to Greattree roots and often contain Glovewort and Spirit Ashes. Usher of Death, Rosus guides the spirits of the dead back to the roots. Interacting with a statue of Rosus produces a trail of blue light that indicates the entrance to the nearest catacombs, provided the player has not already discovered the landmark.

sections.heading: List of Catacombs
sections.markdown: There are 18 Catacombs to find in the Lands Between and three more to discover in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Catacombs contain unique statues of Skeletal Grave Wardens, Imps, Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, Basilisks, and more. Grave Warden statues carry croziers.
- Torrent cannot be summoned inside Catacombs.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bols, Carian Knight** is an optional boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: A hulking troll knight clad in heavy armor and wielding a massive greatsword, Bols was one of the Trolls called into service by the Carians, fighting as a true enchanted knight alongside human comrades. Bols was imprisoned within the Cuckoo's Evergaol in western Liurnia of the Lakes by the Knights of the Cuckoo during the Liurnian Civil War.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: A towering troll knight with slow, sweeping greatsword attacks that create shockwaves. His size makes it easy to pass between his legs and circle to his back. He can summon Greatblade Phalanx blades overhead.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: - Cuckoo's Evergaol (Liurnia of the Lakes)

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown:
- Greatblade Phalanx
- 184,600 Runes

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
- HP: 5,109
- Defense: 110
- Stance: 65
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
- Cannot be Parried
- Strong vs Magic and Frostbite
- Weak to Slash, Poison, Scarlet Rot, and Blood Loss
- Closest Site of Grace: Revenger's Shack
- Multiplayer is not allowed; Spirit Ash summons are disabled

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: Bols, Carian Knight deals Standard damage, Slash damage, Pierce damage, and Magic damage.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Use his size: dodge between his legs and stay on his back side.
- Keep him in view; he can pivot quickly into a follow-up.
- Stay close even for ranged builds; create distance only to reset spacing.
- When he casts Greatblade Phalanx, sprint toward him so the blades pass overhead.
- Shockwaves from slams fan out in front; positioning behind him mitigates most follow-ups.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Caelid Colosseum** is a Location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
An old Colosseum located in northern Caelid, accessed from the Siofra River via the Deep Siofra Well, then traveling north through a ravine. The path is guarded by massive Guardian Golem Archers who fire blue Golem's Magic Arrows.

This arena once hosted gladiatorial combat in honor of the Erdtree during the reign of Lord Godfrey. It was closed during the time of Lord Radagon, and its Duelists were exiled.. However, it is possible that either the colosseum of Caelid managed to remain open or that General Radahn revived the practice of gladiators' fights, since Redmane Freyja was once a gladiator herself and was chosen by Radahn after witnessing her valor in the arena.

The towering Great Jar stands before the arena. Various Knights of the Great Jar may be challenged via red Duelist summon signs. Defeat three champions without dying to unlock the door to the Caelid Colosseum. Interact with the statue of Marika to unlock the activity.

sections.heading: Colosseum PvP
sections.markdown:
Online player-vs-player battles at the Caelid Colosseum allow the use of Spirit Ashes. All three game modes are available:
- Combat Ordeal – Timed free-for-all deathmatch
- Duel Mode – One-on-one duel; no respawns
- United Combat – Timed team deathmatch

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Colossal remains**, also known as **giant skeletons**, **titans**, and other unofficial names, are objects in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
]]
The colossal remains are mountainous skeletal vestiges of a long-extinct species of giant, whose sheer size far surpassed that of Trolls and even Fire Giants. Their immense skulls feature hollow eye sockets large enough to accommodate roosting Giant Crows, and their bones have hardened into solid stone.

These skeletons are embedded into the earth throughout Caelid and the Mountaintops of the Giants. In Caelid, the remains are deeply overgrown with large wooden roots and covered in a thick layer of fungal growth. In contrast, those found in the Mountaintops are fully exposed.

Most of the Mountaintops' colossal skeletons are located on Flame Peak. Two notable examples can be found within a fissure between the Foot of the Forge Site of Grace and the Fire Giant's boss arena.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Only the upper torso and skulls are exposed.
- The skeletons found in Caelid are much larger than those on the Mountaintops.
- The cause of the colossal giants' extinction remains unknown.
- Due to the enormity of their size, it's possible these colossal giants were the original architects of the ancient ruins like the Rauh Ruins along with other landmarks that share the same architectural style, such as the Forge of the Giants and the Divine Towers.
- The giants are the only known creatures large enough to have used the arrowhead that became the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword. It is possible they were the old gods.
- Shadowy titans of similar proportions appear in Limveld on the second Noontide. These colossi appear to be formed from woody vines, and lack bones and upper skulls. Heolstor the Nightlord can reincarnate as one of these arboreal Night Giants.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- In Norse mythology, the Vafþrúðnir claims the earth was formed from the body of .
- In the *Elden Ring* Closed Network Test, heads of similar proportions were present in Limgrave when viewed from Stormveil Castle. Deep lacerations were carved into their stone flesh, which burned like coals.
- A cut dialogue from Enia describes Radahn solely as "the slayer of giants." It is possible the remains in Caelid may once have been related to this cut aspect of his character.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: You Thought This'd Be Serious. Didn't You?** is the 1st chapter of the 1st volume of the *Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree* manga, written and illustrated by Nikiichi Tobita.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The story of the Death of Godwyn, the Shattering War and several Tarnished rising to the call of grace is told. A girl and a steed, Torrent, arrive in a cave in search for a potential Elden Lord, with an unconscious tarnished lying naked, on the floor. She leaves behind two sacred flasks in the hopes that they'll serve him on his journey. The tarnished is next seen exiting a mausoleum to be greeted by White Mask Varré, who's unusual mannerisms unnerve him. Varré recommends that the tarnished starts his journey to Stormveil, an advice he takes openly and proceeds to attempt asking the nearby golden knight for a ride to the castle, only to be met with violence. Meanwhile in Stormveil Castle, Godrick the Grafted is judging recent grafting as presented by Gatekeeper Gostoc. Finding them lackluster, Godrick urges the servants to work more collaboratively in creating new designs before leaving. The tarnished is then seen despairing over the ruthlessness of every living thing he comes across only to be met by the girl who left him the flasks, Melina, offering him an accord.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Confessors** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The confessors were Tarnished who once received the guidance of grace, but willfully ignored the path it laid before them. In doing so, they lost the ability to perceive it again. Though their grace was never restored, they found renewed purpose as covert operatives serving the Two Fingers at the Roundtable Hold.

These assassins operated in darkness, tasked with eliminating other Tarnished who had strayed from grace. Their covert missions often led them beyond the Lands Between, where they served churches aligned with the Fingers’ doctrine as wandering priests and spies.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Dressed in black leather to blend seamlessly into the night, confessors use their talents to eliminate enemies of the Fingers and rogue Tarnished alike. They employ subterfuge to distract and confound their enemies, setting the stage for a deadly ambush. Using ritual implements, they masked the sound of their movements, causing many paranoid Tarnished to dread total silence.

One of the most prominent head confessors, Crepus, wielded a long-range black-key crossbow, fitted with spiral-tipped bolts that injected scarlet rot deep into his targets. Another assassin, Rileigh the Idle, also used the black-key crossbow along with a dagger fashioned from the stinger of a great scorpion.

The confessor emblem is a black-key.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Buffs** are effects applied by a Tarnished to either themself or to themself and their allies, and are used to strengthen offence or defence.

They primarily come in three categories: Weapon Buffs, Body Buffs, and Aura Buffs.

sections.heading: Weapon Buffs
sections.markdown:
All Weapon Buffs are self-targeted, and almost all of them have only offensive benefits, with very few exceptions. They cannot be applied to any type of ranged weapon or casting implement, and only a few specific ones can be used on shields.

It's possible to keep two weapons buffed at the same time by two-handing the left-hand weapon and using either a Grease or a Skill on it, then stopping the two-handing so that the right-hand weapon also can be buffed with either a Grease or a Skill. It isn't necessary to use the same buff category for both weapons.

Some weapons are buffable and some aren't. As a general rule, weapons upgraded with Smithing Stones are buffable while weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones aren't buffable unless their innate skill grants them a weapon buff. Exceptions to this rule are the Crystal Knife and Ivory Sickle, two Smithing Stone weapons that aren't buffable, and the Bloodhound's Fang and Varré's Bouquet, two Somber Smithing Stone weapon that are buffable.

Additionally, weapons equipped with affinities that aren't either Standard, Heavy, Keen, or Quality also aren't buffable except for with the Skills that are compatible with those affinities, with no exceptions.

For Weapon Buffs that are also either Sorceries or Incantations, they can only be cast on right-handed weapons (or left-handed shields for the shield-specific ones).

sections.heading: Body Buffs
sections.markdown: Most Body Buffs are self-targeted and defensive in their benefits, but some, primarily those that are the upgraded form of weaker Body Buffs, also grant their benefits to nearby allies. A scant few are instead focused on increasing the caster's offensive strength.

sections.heading: Aura Buffs
sections.markdown: All Aura Buffs target both the caster and their nearby allies, and most, with the exception of some offense-only Aura Buffs, provide both offensive and defensive benefits.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Commander Gaius** is an optional boss in Shadow of the Erdtree encountered outside the backdoor of the Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Commander Gaius was a noted warrior and military strategist who rode a giant boar as his steed. Gaius studied gravitational magic from an Alabaster Lord. He was a fellow student of Radahn, a future demigod. He also befriended Messmer the Impaler, as both had in common that they were cursed from birth. The pair were as elder brothers to Radahn, with whom Gaius had formed a friendly rivalry.
When Messmer embarked on the purge of the Land of Shadow on Queen Marika the Eternal's orders, Gaius would join him and serve as the commander of his soldiers. He was never without his boar. Even when Marika abandoned Messmer, Gaius remained steadfast, guarding the backdoor of Shadow Keep. It was here that he would meet his end at the hands of a Tarnished champion.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.markdown: Commander Gaius is an albinauric without legs who rides a heavily armored, great-tusked boar. Gaius wears black iron armor patterned to represent fallen seeds and wields the Sword Lance. He was cursed by his Albinauric heritage and as such was doomed to lose the use of his legs.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown: Commander Gaius will charge with his boar to try to run you over. This can be dodge by jumping over with torrent or dodging at a very exact moment. He also uses gravity magic to attack enemies that are too far away.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Wears Gaius's Helm, Gaius's Armor, Gaius's Gauntlets, and Gaius's Greaves
- Wields Sword Lance
- Casts Blades of Stone
- Gaius serves as a foil to Royal Knight Loretta, who hid her Albinauric nature from her compatriots.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Briar Set** is an armor set in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Each piece can be purchased from Finger Reader Enia after defeating Elemer of the Briar in The Shaded Castle.
- The regular chestpiece can be bought for 6,000 runes and the other 3 pieces cost 4,000 runes each, for a total cost of 18,000 runes for the entire set.
- The altered chest piece can be attained by altering the regular chest piece with the Tailoring Tools.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The set has good overall physical defenses, with a slight weakness toward Strike damage, and good Fire defense, mirrored by a significantly lower Lightning defense. It also offers strong resistance against Blood Loss and Frostbite due to its high Robustness, with decent resistance against Poison and Scarlet Rot from its somewhat lower Immunity.
- Each armor piece causes a small amount of damage (25 points from either chest piece and 18 from each other armor piece, for 79 damage total when the whole set is worn) when the wearer touches an enemy while rolling or using the skills Quickstep or Bloodhound's Step.
 - Note that this is before any damage reduction is applied, usually resulting in less than 15 damage being dealt when the whole set is worn.
 - While the damage is extremely low, it still has significant utility: weaker enemies can be lightly staggered by the damage as if they were hit by a Dagger or Straight Sword, and other players can be finished off or have their Opaline Bubbletear effect removed.
 - The effect stacks with the Mantle of Thorns sorcery, which will also add some minimal Blood Loss build-up to rolls.
- The total Poise of 47 is just short of the common PvE breakpoint of 51 to resist lighter enemy attacks. Swapping out a piece or two to reach that level is a good idea unless the damage from dodging is extremely attractive to you.

- Excellent Immunity and Robustness grants high resistance to Poison, Scarlet Rot, Blood Loss, and Frostbite.
- Excellent Strike and Pierce defense, the former of which is quite unusual on a metal armor set.
- Surprisingly enough the Set doesn't carry any of the Fire weakness the associated enemies have. Additionally, it only has a minor weakness to Lightning compared to other sets made of metal.

A rare gravesite flower, the Ghostflame Bloom, is said to grow in here, blossoming into the cold ghostflame. sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The chair-crypts are towering stone thrones of religious significance constructed by the Nox in ancient times. They appear in the Eternal Cities and Sellia, Town of Sorcery. These chairs are carved from stone and decorated with ornamental floral patterns, including a large inverted flower on their backrests. Some are occupied by giant mummies. Beneath each throne lies a chamber containing a chest with valuable Nox relics. Occupied chair-crypts also contain a Great Ghost Glovewort.

sections.heading: Locations

There are four chair-crypts in the Lands Between:

1. Sellia, Town of Sorcery ( Chair-Crypt of Sellia) — an unoccupied throne guarded by a Nox Swordstress & Nox Monk; contains Lusat's Glintstone Staff
1. Nokron, Eternal City ( Night's Sacred Ground) — an occupied throne guarded by a Troll Mimic Tear and several Mimic Tears; contains the Fingerslayer Blade and a Great Ghost Glovewort
1. Nokstella, Eternal City ( Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella) — an occupied throne guarded by Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella; contains a Great Ghost Glovewort
1. Nokstella, Eternal City ( Nokstella, Eternal City) — an unoccupied throne guarded by a Nox Swordstress and two Mimic Tears; contains the Moon of Nokstella
1. Noklateo, the Shrouded City () — an occupied throne guarded by a Naturalborn of the Void; contains the Favor of Noklateo, the Shrouded City

sections.markdown: The **Cerulean Coast** is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Cerulean Coast is located on the Southern Shore of the Realm of Shadow. It is connected to Charo's Hidden Grave, Foot of the Jagged Peak, Gravesite Plain, and the Stone Coffin Fissure. The area is revealed on the Shadow Realm map when Map: Southern Shore has been collected.

The Cerulean Coast is accessible via the Pillar Path Cross south of Castle Ensis. Adventurers can traverse this region by heading north to cliffs, descending via rock formations, and proceeding south through Ellac River Cave. Glowing blue flowers and massive stone arks signify the Cerulean Coast.

The northeast Cerulean Coast contains the Finger Ruins of Rhia, and the Southern Nameless Mausoleum lies on an island to the west. A rocky southern peninsula hides a deep tunnel leading to the Stone Coffin Fissure legacy dungeon, which remains locked by a Miquella's Haligtree seal until Miquella discards his Great Rune. This story event is triggered by entering the Shadow Keep or crossing the bridge east of Bonny Village.

sections.heading: Background

These stone vesels house the Congealed Putrescence of ancient, tainted life, once purified in ghostflame by the deathbirds long ago. The blue flowers are contrasted by a sea of luminous crimson lilies on the plateau above, said to be the home of the Tibia Mariners and the hidden grave of Charo. Deep underground, below both fields, wilts St. Trina's Garden of Deep Purple.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Church of the Bud is a sacred site of unclear purpose constructed by the Hornsent within the western half of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The church features distinctive spiral pillars topped with decorative buds. The Scarlet Buds found here were originally a different color, untainted by the scarlet rot. Behind the church, a stone platform supports the Sealing Tree that veils Enir-Ilim in shadow. This tree can only be burned with Messmer's Kindling.

The church was the only building in Rauh to be razed by Messmer's army during the crusade. Romina sat on the ground in shock, clutching the bud, as the church burned around her. In her despair, she uncovered a divine essence within the ashes and weaved it into the scarlet rot. Her actions imbued the church's flowers with scarlet rot, caused local Spider Scorpions to grow in size, and transformed the landscape surrounding the Church of the Bud into a scarlet rot swamp. After the Battle of Aeonia, Romina summoned and soothed Malenia's unwanted butterflies. Now, she uses her Poleblade of the Bud to perform a long-forgotten purification ritual.

The Site of Grace is unlocked after Romina, Saint of the Bud is defeated.

sections.markdown: Butterflies** are a concept in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Butterflies were thin-feathered insects known for their large, often brightly colored wings and fluttering flight. An aspect of the primordial Crucible, they held divine significance for the denizens of the Lands Between, and were used in purification rituals at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh in antiquity.

Each connected to a Demigod child of Queen Marika and Radagon, four strains of sacred butterfly appeared during the age of the Erdtree: Black Pyrefly (Messmer), Smoldering Butterfly (Melina), Nascent Butterfly (St. Trina and Miquella), and Aeonian Butterfly (Malenia).

When Malenia unleashed the scarlet rot at the Battle of Aeonia, scarlet butterflies emerged and became her wings, granting immense strength. Despite this, she later rejected them, just as she did the Servants of Rot. Only upon her transformation into Malenia, Goddess of Rot—when the Scarlet Aeonia blooms a second time—do butterflies return as her wings. The forsaken scarlet butterflies were left to roam the Swamp of Aeonia or were taken in by Romina, Saint of the Bud, who summoned scarlet rot after Messmer's crusade reached the Church of the Bud. Like the Kindred of Rot, these butterflies turned bright pink when they were embraced by Romina.

sections.heading: Notes

sections.markdown: Church of the Crusade** is a location within the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The Church of the Crusade is a church featuring a headless statue of Queen Marika the Eternal on the Scadu Altus. It is built on a hill southwest of the Shadow Keep and northwest of the Highroad Cross Site of Grace. A member of the Forager Brood nurses an injury just outside the church. It may be healed by placing either a Warming Stone or Sunwarmth Stone and resting at any Site of Grace. This is one of two locations at which Fire Knight Queelign Invades to ward away those stripped of the Erdtree's grace.
